name: Spain
summary_text: Spain is a very safe destination for transgender visitors. The 2023 "Trans Law" established legal gender recognition by self-identification and broad anti-discrimination protections, and a parallel penal-code reform made gender identity an explicit hate-crime ground — with real enforcement, including convictions carrying transphobia aggravation. There is no legal restriction on trans people using bathrooms or facilities matching their presentation, and the national tourism industry actively promotes Spain as an LGBTQ destination. Acceptance is high in cities and tourist regions, though attitudes can be more conservative in some rural areas. Political debate around trans rights is heated, and some regional governments (Madrid, 2023) have rolled back regional protections — signals of a polarised climate rather than changes to a visitor's everyday legal position. Documented incidents exist: harassment and verbal-abuse prosecutions, a high-profile local-police transphobia case in Benidorm, and gangs targeting queer tourists through dating apps (mainly gay men) in tourist zones — the latter being a general safety caution for app-based meetups anywhere.

sources.title: BOE-A-2023-5366 Ley 4/2023, de 28 de febrero, para la igualdad real y efectiva de las personas trans y para la garantía de los derechos de las personas LGTBI.
sources.claim_summary: Official text (BOE) of Ley 4/2023 (28 February 2023), 'for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of the rights of LGTBI people': establishes self-ID legal gender recognition (16+, no diagnosis), broad anti-discrimination guarantees, employment and health measures, and an LGTBI equality strategy.

sources.title: Victory in Fight for Gender Recognition in Spain | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Feb 2023): 'Victory in Fight for Gender Recognition in Spain' — hails Spain's self-ID gender-recognition law as a hard-won victory after years of activism.

sources.title: Hate Crimes and LGBTI Protection: Which Law Changed What
sources.claim_summary: Spanish criminal-law firm analysis (June 2026): disentangles three statutes - what Law 4/2023 does and does not do; the discrimination aggravating factor of Article 22.4 of the Penal Code (gender identity/expression motives); and the hate offences of Article 510 CP extended to trans/LGBTI people.

sources.title: UK and Spain bathroom break rules « Euro Weekly News
sources.claim_summary: Euro Weekly News (July 2026): contrast piece for expats/travellers - unlike the UK after its Supreme Court ruling, Spain has no legal restriction on trans people using facilities matching their gender; using gendered facilities matching presentation is legal.

sources.title: LGBTQIA+ travel in Spain | Intrepid Travel US
sources.claim_summary: Intrepid Travel country guide ('Is Spain safe for LGBTQIA+ travellers?'): Spain is a safe, welcoming destination with marriage equality and protective laws; conservative views persist in rural areas; trans people widely accepted though gender-identity discrimination still occurs.

sources.title: Safety and Diversity: Spain as a reference for LGB… | tourspain.es in english
sources.claim_summary: Turespaña (national tourism institute) B2B page: Spain as a reference destination for LGBTQ+ tourism - inclusive policies, specialised accommodation and events; cites the Homophobic Climate Index and Travel Safety Index ranking Spain among the safest and most welcoming destinations.

sources.title: Condena pionera en Vigo: agravante por transfobia a unas amenazas enviadas por WhatsApp
sources.claim_summary: La Razón (July 2026, in Spanish): pioneering conviction in Vigo applying the transphobia aggravating factor - WhatsApp threats; €300 fine. Shows the new hate-crime framework is being enforced.

sources.title: Seis meses de cárcel por perseguir, insultar y grabar a una persona trans en Valencia - Observatorio de delitos de odio y discriminación
sources.claim_summary: Observatorio de delitos de odio (Jan 2026, in Spanish): six-month prison sentence for a youth gang that pursued, insulted and filmed a trans person in Valencia (including minors among the perpetrators).

sources.title: Safety and security - Spain travel advice - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Foreign travel advice for Spain: safety and security (terrorism threat, crime). General travel advice, not trans-specific.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Spain - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia overview: comprehensive LGBT rights in Spain - same-sex marriage since 2005, adoption, strong discrimination protections, bias-motivated speech/violence provisions, transgender and intersex rights sections, conversion-therapy restrictions, and very positive public opinion.

sources.title: This Is How 23 Countries Feel About Transgender Rights
sources.claim_summary: BuzzFeed News/Ipsos/Williams Institute global survey (Dec 2016) on transgender rights across 23 countries: Spain and Sweden rank at the top for support for trans rights (bathroom access, surgery, marriage, parenting, discrimination protection); one-quarter of Americans say people should never be allowed to change legal gender - comparative public-attitudes data.
